707996.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kúrios, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱewh₁- (“to swell; to spread out; to be strong; to prevail”). By surface analysis, κῦρος (kûros, “supremacy”) + -ιος (-ĭos, adjective suffix).

707923.t: Unknown. Determination is complicated by the fact that the word is similar to Ancient Greek καλύπτω (kalúptō, “to cover”) in both form and sense, thus indicating possible analogical influence in both directions.

707946.t: Beekes attributes it to a Mediterranean substrate, probably Pre-Greek.

707910.t: From κρι-, the root of κρίνω (krī́nō, “to decide, judge”), + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

707957.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *kúklos, *kʷókʷlos, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷékʷlos (“circle, wheel”).

707912.t: Unknown. Ionic word for "lizard" (common being σαύρα (saúra)), perhaps from κρόκη (krókē, “pebble”) + δρῖλος (drîlos, “worm”), because crocodiles like resting on flat stones.

707926.t: According to Beekes, the word is Pre-Greek — which Beekes claims is the case for all Greek words with the -αλλο- suffix.

707905.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kríňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *kri-n-yé-ti, from *krey- (“to sift, separate”). Cognates include English rinse, Latin cernō (“to separate, discern”), and Welsh gogrynu.

707949.t: Difficult to trace. The word passed to and from a number of languages (compare Latin cubus (“mass, quantity; cube”)).

707952.t: Assumed to be from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kewh₁- (“to perceive, pay attention”) and therefore related to κοέω (koéō), Latin caveō, Sanskrit कवि (kaví, “wise, poet, seer, sage”), Persian کی (kay, “poet-king”), Lithuanian kavoti (“safeguard, tend”), Old…

707917.t: Unclear. Usually derived from κρότος (krótos, “beating”), as "beating of the veins in the temples", while Furnée instead connects it with κόρση (kórsē, “temple”), as well as, more distantly, κρόσσαι (króssai, “steps of pyramid”).

707913.t: A Semitic loanword. Compare Akkadian 𒌑𒆪𒄀𒆸𒈾 (/⁠kurkanū⁠/), Arabic كُرْكُم (kurkum), and Hebrew כרכום (karkom).

707938.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tḱey- (“to settle”). Cognates include Sanskrit क्षेति॑ (kṣéti), Avestan 𐬱𐬀𐬉𐬌𐬙𐬌 (šaēⁱti) and, via Iranian borrowing, Old Armenian շէն (šēn).

707989.t: Related to, and perhaps derived from, κυφός (kuphós, “bent forward, hunchbacked”), which Beekes suspects is of Pre-Greek origin; see there for more.

707963.t: Perhaps from a Proto-Indo-European *ḱewk- (“white”), with cognates including Sanskrit शोचति (śócati, “to shine, suffer”) and शुक्र (śukrá, “bright, white”), and possibly Old Norse Hǿnir (“god associated with swans and storks”).

707909.t: From κριτήρ (krĭtḗr, “interpreter”) + -ιον (-ĭon), from κρίνω (krī́nō, “I discern, judge”).

707982.t: Of loanword origin, probably from a Mediterranean Pre-Greek language; compare Hebrew כּוֺפֶר /כֹּפֶר (kōp̱er, “pitch, tar; henna”), Aramaic כּוּפְרָא / ܟܘܦܪܐ (kūp̄rā, “pitch, tar; henna”), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎔𐎗 (kpr, “henna”), Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀞𐀫 (ku-pa-ro,…

707902.t: Traditionally derived from a reduplicated form of Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to bend, turn”).

707900.t: Uncertain. Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰérsdʰ-o/eh₂-, with cognates including Latin hordeum, Old High German gersta, but there are phonetic difficulties with this.

707940.t: From κτίζω (ktízō, “to found, to build”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

707973.t: Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀖𐀜 (ku-mi-no), borrowed from Semitic, compare Ge'ez ከሚን (kämin), ካሚን (kamin), ከሙን (kämun), ከሜን (kämen), Arabic كَمُّون (kammūn), Hebrew כַּמֹּון (kammōn), Aramaic כַּמֹּונָֹא / ܩܰܡܽܘܢܳܐ (kammōnā, “cumin”), ultimately from…

707993.t: Feminine form of κύριος (kū́rĭos, “lord; ruler; possessor”).

707999.t: Unclear. The comparison with Latin curvus (“curved”) presupposes that the Greek adjective continues a reduced grade *kʷr-to-s with u coloring, which is phonetically difficult and places the comparison in doubt.

707944.t: Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin due to the presence of variations and rejects a derivation from κυέω (kŭéō); possibly connected to Classical Syriac ܓܘܡܐ (gūmā), Jewish Babylonian Aramaic גוגמא, גגמא (“bean”).

707942.t: Reminiscent of δοῦπος (doûpos, “thud”), but further details are unknown. The variation between voiced and unvoiced stop suggests Pre-Greek origin.

707904.t: Unknown; presumedly of foreign or substrate origin.

707988.t: Identical to Hebrew כֹּפֶר / כּוֺפֶר (kōp̱er, “pitch, tar; henna”), Aramaic כּוּפְרָא / ܟܘܦܪܐ (kūp̄rā, “pitch, tar; henna”), Ugaritic 𐎋𐎔𐎗 (kpr, “henna”), Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀞𐀫 (ku-pa-ro, debatable plant), Coptic ⲕⲟⲩⲡⲣ (koupr, “henna”), Demotic Egyptian qwpr…

707939.t: κτίζω (ktĭ́zō, “found, build”) + -σις (-sĭs). Cognate with Sanskrit क्षितिज (kṣitija).

707932.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tk-éh₁- (“acquisition”), from Proto-Indo-European *tek- (“to take by the hand; to receive, obtain”).

707943.t: Uncertain. Sometimes connected with κύαρ (kúar, “eye of a needle”) but according to Beekes of Pre-Greek origin.

707920.t: According to Beekes, from Proto-Indo-European *krows- (“push, bump, strike, break”), zero grade *krus-.

707911.t: From κρέκω (krékō, “to weave”) + -η (-ē, abstract noun suffix). The former is from Proto-Indo-European *krek- (“to weave”), see also Serbo-Croatian kresati, English reel.

707998.t: Possibly from a Proto-Hellenic *kū́ros + -όω (-óō). Related to κύριος (kúrios).

707914.t: A similar word for "onion" and "garlic" is found in Proto-West Germanic *hramusō (“onion, garlic”), Proto-Slavic *čermъša (“ramson”) and Middle Irish crem (“wild garlic”), suggesting a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *kermus- (“wild garlic”).

707972.t: From κύμβη (kúmbē, “hollow of a vessel”), with a suffix -αλον which is found also in κρόταλον (krótalon, “rattle”).

707930.t: From κρύπτω (krúptō, “hide, conceal”) + -ιος (-ios, “pertaining to, belonging to”)

707918.t: By surface analysis, κρότος (krótos) + -έω (-éō). Probably from Proto-Hellenic *krotéō, from Proto-Indo-European *krotéyeti, a causative verb from the root *kret- (“to rattle”).

707967.t: A secondary present form of κυλίνδω (kŭlíndō, “to roll, turn over”).
